title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: recent incidents AND load tests showed unexplained token-level cost spikes attributable to KV cache churn and suboptimal batching behavior. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, end-to-end tracing spans for cache lookups/misses/hits, updated Grafana dashboards with cost/latency breakdowns per model and cache tier, and alert tuning to reduce noisy paging at high QPS. Goal: give SRE and product teams visibility into per-token economics and trends so we can tune batching, cache TTLs, and eviction policies without blind rollouts.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds new Prometheus metrics: redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_evictions_total, redwood_token_cost_estimate_bytes and redwood_token_latency_histogram (labels: model, deployment_tier, cache_tier, shard).
- Instruments KV cache code path with tracing spans (cache.lookup, cache.populate, cache.evict) and attaches token/seq metadata to spans.
- Updates the existing token-level dashboard: adds KV cache panel group (hit rate, miss rate, evictions), cost/latency waterfall per-token, per-model heatmaps, and a top-talkers table for high-cost prompts.
- Adds a dedicated alert rule set with tuned thresholds and recovery windows: KVCacheHighEvictionRate, TokenCostSpike, TokenLatencyRegression. Alerts include runbook links and suggested mitigations (increase cache TTL, adjust batching policy, fallback to cheaper model variant).
- Backfills a small migration to populate historical cache-miss ratios for the last 7 days (best-effort) for dashboard continuity.
- Adds integration tests for new metrics and tracing spans, and a dashboard JSON export for review.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics added and registered with descriptive help strings
- [x] Tracing spans added and validated with unit tests
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panels committed
- [x] Alert rules added and sanity-tested in staging
- [x] Runbooks linked and basic remediation steps documented
- [x] Load-tested at 2x production QPS in perf-canary

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for metrics and span attributes added in redwood/serving/runtime/cache_test.go (coverage ~84% for the cache package).
- e2e integration in staging shows KVCacheHighEvictionRate firing only under synthetic eviction scenarios; TokenCostSpike alert triggered as expected when we injected a high-cost prompt generator.
- Load test: perf-canary run with 2x QPS for 6 hours showed stable CPU and memory; token-level cost estimates matched billing-derived estimates within 4% error margin.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind feature flag observability.kv_token_metrics (default: off).
- Roll to staging -> internal beta -> gradual rollout to 10% production -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on increased 5xxs or latency regressions.

Notes:
- The new metrics increase cardinality due to model+deployment_tier+cache_tier labels; we intentionally limited label values (small set of tiers) and added cardinality safety checks in the metrics registration code.
- The migration backfill is best-effort and will not block rollout if it times out.

Related: ENG-1281 (token-level observability initiative), SRE-342 (incident postmortem to reduce KV churn), SUP-987 (customer reported cost spike).
